chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manquri, from Sufyan ibn Ayyinah, from Al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them).

He said: The last advice that Al-Khizr gave to Moses ibn Imran (peace be upon them) was that he said to him: 'Do not reproach anyone for a sin. And the most beloved of deeds to God, the Exalted, are three: moderation in wealth, forgiveness when in power, and gentleness with the servants of God. And whoever is gentle with someone in this world, God the Exalted will be gentle with him on the Day of Resurrection. And the head of wisdom is the fear of God, the Blessed and Exalted.'

key_terms.لَا تُعَيِّرَنَّ أَحَدًا بِذَنْبٍ: Do not reproach anyone for a sin
key_terms.وَالرِّفْقُ بِعِبَادِ اللَّهِ: Gentleness with the servants of God

ai.seo_question: What are the three most beloved deeds to God according to the advice of Al-Khizr to Moses?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration preserves the final testament of Al-Khizr to Moses, emphasizing that moderation in prosperity, forgiveness when capable, and gentleness toward creation are paramount. It establishes a reciprocal divine mercy where human *rifq* (gentleness) invites Allah’s mercy on the Day of Judgment, culminating in the identification of *khauf Allah* (fear of God) as the head of wisdom, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-83 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Minqari, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Ayyineh, on the authority of Al-Zuhra, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB), “

The last advice of al-Khizr (MGB) to Moses - the son of Imran (MGB) was as follows: ‘Never blame anyone for their sins. The best deeds in the Opinion of God are the following three deeds: moderation at times of being wealthy; forgiving at times of being in power; and being kind to the servants of God (i.e. the people). If anyone treats others with kindness in this world, God the Honorable the Exalted will treat him with kindness on the Resurrection Day. The foremost form of wisdom is fearing the Blessed the Sublime God.’”
